content: The text provided is a list of references formatted in a highly fragmented and non-standard way. It appears to be a bibliography or citation list for academic or medical research articles, primarily focused on wheelchair provision, training, assistive technology, and related healthcare topics. 1. A scoping review protocol was developed to explore the perspectives of educators and healthcare professionals across lowto high-resource settings regarding assistive technology and rehabilitation. This was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2020. 2. Rusek CT, Kleven M, Walker C, Walker K, Heeb R, and Morgan KA conducted a qualitative analysis on the perspectives of inpatient rehabilitation clinicians regarding the state of manual wheelchair training. Their findings were published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2021. 3. Goldberg M, Rushton P, Kirby RL, Muñera S, Kandavel K, Pearlman J, and colleagues reviewed the content of wheelchair service provision in professional rehabilitation organizations' standards documents and contemporary initiatives. This rapid review was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2022. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF published a manual in 2020 on public procurement of assistive products, accessories, spare parts, and related services. This document provides detailed specifications and usage guidelines for assistive products. 5. Kirby RL, Miller WC, Routhier F, Demers L, Mihailidis A, Polgar JM, and others conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a wheelchair skills training program for powered wheelchair users. Their study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. 6. Kirby RL, Mitchell D, Sabharwal S, McCranie M, and Nelson AL investigated the impact of manual wheelchair skills training for community-dwelling veterans with spinal cord injuries. Their randomized controlled trial was published in PLOS ONE in 2016. 7. Giesbrecht EM and Miller WC conducted a feasibility randomized controlled trial to assess the effect of an mHealth wheelchair skills training program for older adults. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2019. 8. Miller WC, Best KL, Eng JJ, and Routhier F explored the influence of peer-led wheelchair training on skills and participation among older adults. Their clinical outcomes were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2019. 9. Ozturk A and Ucsular FD evaluated the effectiveness of a wheelchair skills training program for community-living manual wheelchair users in Turkey. Their randomized controlled trial was published in Clinical Rehabilitation in 2011. 10. Jan YK, Jones MA, Rabadi MH, Foreman RD, and Thiessen A studied the effects of wheelchair tilt-in-space and recline angles on skin perfusion over the ischial tuberosity in individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their research was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2010. 11. Worobey LA, Kirby RL, Heinemann AW, Krobot EA, Dyson-Hudson TA, Cowan RE, and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of group wheelchair skills training for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. 12. Charlton K, Murray C, Boucaut R, and Berndt A facilitated manual wheelchair skills training for individuals with lower limb amputations using a group process. Their pilot study, employing a nested mixed-methods design, was published in the Australian Occupational Therapy Journal in 2021. 13. MacGillivray MK, Sawatzky BJ, Miller WC, Routhier F, and Kirby RL demonstrated that individualized powered wheelchair skills training improves goal satisfaction. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2018. 14. Mountain AD, Kirby RL, Smith C, Eskes G, and Thompson K conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess powered wheelchair skills training for individuals with stroke. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2014. 15. Tasiejski T, Wilski M, Urbanski P, and others evaluated the effects of a community peer-based wheelchair skills training camp in Morocco. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2021. 16. Kirby RL, Mifflen NJ, Thibault DL, Smith C, Best KL, Thompson KJ, and colleagues examined the manual wheelchair-handling skills of caregivers and the impact of training. Their research was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2004. 17. Worobey LA, McKernan G, Toro M, Pearlman J, Cowan RE, Heinemann AW, and others conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of group wheelchair maintenance training for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2021. 18. Rigot SK, DiGiovine KM, Boninger ML, Hibbs R, Smith I, and Worobey LA assessed the effectiveness of a web-based direct-to-user transfer training program through a randomized controlled trial. Their study was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2021. 19. Rice LA, Sung JH, Keane K, Peterson E, and Sosnoff JJ conducted a pilot study on a brief fall prevention intervention for manual wheelchair users with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in the Journal of Spinal Cord Medicine in 2020. 20. Sawatzky B, Rushton PW, Denison I, and McDonald R piloted a wheelchair skills training program for children. Their study was published in the Australian Occupational Therapy Journal in 2012. 21. Sawatzky B, Mortenson WB, and Wong S explored the learning process for using a rear-mounted power assist for manual wheelchairs. Their findings were published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2018. 22. Beaudoin M, Best KL, Raymond E, and Routhier F evaluated the influence of a peer-led community-based wheelchair skills training program, Roulez avec confiance, on manual wheelchair users. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2021. 23. Sakakibara BM, Miller WC, Souza M, Nikolova V, and Best KL conducted a pilot study to improve confidence in manual wheelchair use among older adults through wheelchair skills training. Their findings were published in the Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2013. 24. Tu CJ, Liu L, Wang W, Du HP, Wang YM, Xu YB, and colleagues systematically reviewed the effectiveness and safety of wheelchair skills training programs in improving wheelchair skills capacity. Their review was published in Clinical Rehabilitation in 2017. 25. Keeler L, Kirby RL, Parker K, McLean KD, and Hayden JA conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness of the Wheelchair Skills Training Program. Their findings were published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2019.
